login.title: Sign in
login.subtitle: Use your domain account.
login.totp-hint: 6 digits from your app, or a recovery code.

home.title: Overview
home.node-hidden: You may not view node information.
home.run-job: Collect node information as a job
home.placeholder: Phase 1 placeholder: users, groups and policies arrive in Phase 2.

error.title: Something went wrong
error.forbidden: You don't have permission to view this page.

setup.title: Set up OpenDC
setup.subtitle: This host is not part of a domain yet.
setup.token-help: Enter the one-time setup token. It was shown when OpenDC was installed; on the host you can print it again with:
setup.role-primary: The first domain controller of a new domain
setup.role-primary-hint: Creates a new Active Directory domain.
setup.role-dc: An additional domain controller of an existing domain
setup.role-dc-hint: Joins a domain whose first DC already runs.
setup.fqdn-hint: e.g. dc1.ad.example.com; the part after the first dot is the domain.
setup.domain: DNS domain of the AD domain
setup.domain-hint: A domain you own; the Kerberos realm is its upper-case form.
setup.netbios-hint: Up to 15 characters; shown as DOMAIN\user.
setup.dc-host-hint: IP address of a running DC of the domain (a name only if this host can already resolve it).
setup.forwarders-hint: Upstream DNS servers for Internet names (comma-separated).
setup.ntp-hint: Optional; empty keeps the distribution's NTP pool.
setup.id-base-hint: POSIX IDs are this value plus the RID.
setup.level-hint: 2008_R2 works with every supported Samba version.
setup.admin-help: Choose the password of the domain Administrator. Store it safely: it is the key to the whole domain.
setup.pw-complexity: Use three of: lower case, upper case, digits, symbols.
setup.confirm-primary: {{fqdn}} becomes the first domain controller of the new domain {{domain}}. Samba, DNS and the time service on this host are reconfigured.
setup.confirm-dc: {{fqdn}} joins {{domain}} as a domain controller. Samba, DNS and the time service on this host are reconfigured.
setup.running: Setting up… This takes a few minutes. Keep this page open.
setup.done-primary: The domain {{domain}} is up and {{fqdn}} is its first DC. Log in as Administrator.
setup.done-dc: {{fqdn}} is now a domain controller of {{domain}}.
setup.already: This host is already set up (domain {{domain}}).

dir.title: Directory
dir.protected-hint: Protected object: changes need a tier-0 role and a typed confirmation.
dir.protected-banner: This is a protected (tier-0) object. Changes need a tier-0 role, and you must type its name to confirm.
dir.generated-help: This password is shown only once. Give it to the user through a safe channel.
dir.search: Search by name, account or mail
dir.f-password-hint: Leave empty to generate a strong password.
dir.f-mustChange: Must change the password at next login
dir.tier0-members: This group is protected (tier 0). Changing its members changes who administers the domain.
dir.delete-body: {{name}} will be deleted. Deleted objects can only be restored from the AD recycle bin or a backup.
dir.delete-ou-body: {{name}} and everything in it will be deleted.
dir.bulk-done: Done: {{done}} changed, {{failed}} failed (see the audit log for details).

domain.title: Domain
domain.name: DNS name
domain.fsmo-transfer-help: Moves the selected roles to the DC you are connected to. The current holder must be online.
domain.fsmo-seize-warning: Seize only when the current holder is gone for good and will never come back. A DC that comes back after a seizure corrupts the domain.
domain.fsmo-force: Seize without trying a transfer first
domain.fsmo-confirm: Type the role names to confirm: {{phrase}}
domain.level-warning: Raising the functional level can't be undone. Every DC must support the new level.

rbac.title: Roles and permissions
rbac.tier0-hint: May hold tier-0 permissions and change protected objects (Domain Admins and the like). Grant sparingly.

pwp.title: Password policies
pwp.default-hint: Applies to every account that no fine-grained policy covers.
pwp.psos-hint: Apply to users and groups directly. With several, the lowest precedence wins. OU-linked policies arrive with policies in Phase 3.
pwp.name: Name
pwp.complexity-hint: Three of: upper case, lower case, digits, symbols; not containing the account name.

imp.title: Import users
imp.help: Upload a CSV file with a header row (comma or semicolon separated). The "sam" column is required; other columns: givenName, sn, displayName, mail, title, department, company, office, telephoneNumber, mobile, password, groups (names separated by |), enabled, accountExpires. Run a dry run first: nothing changes until you apply.

tpl.title: User templates
tpl.name: Name
tpl.placeholders: Values may use {firstname}, {lastname}, {sam} and {domain}, e.g. mail {firstname}.{lastname}@example.com.

acc.title: Account of {{name}}
acc.totp-on: An authenticator app is set up. Sign-ins and tier-0 actions ask for its code.
acc.totp-off: No second factor is set up. It is recommended for every administrator.
acc.totp-required: Your role is tier 0: a second factor is required.
acc.totp-secret-help: Add this secret to an authenticator app (TOTP, 6 digits, 30 seconds), then enter the code it shows. The secret is shown only now.
acc.totp-uri: Or import this link into an app that accepts otpauth:// links:
acc.totp-done: The authenticator app is set up.
acc.recovery-help: Recovery codes: each works once if you lose the device. Store them safely; they are shown only now.
acc.mfa-help: Your role administers the domain (tier 0), so it needs an authenticator app in addition to your password. Set one up to continue.
acc.reauth-help: This action changes tier-0 objects. Confirm your password (and authenticator code) to continue.
acc.tokens-help: Tokens let the opendc CLI and scripts act as you (Authorization: Bearer). They never carry tier-0 rights.
acc.token-created: Token created. Copy it now: it is shown only once.
